Everyone's savings were dwindling, and the winter for the live-streaming industry had arrived.
Besides his live-streaming platform, other platforms, large and small, were also operating.
And in less than a month, nearly 70% had gone bankrupt—a truly outrageous situation.
Fortunately, although his platform's revenue was declining,
it remained number one.
Furthermore, the platform had a good reputation; comments were controlled, preventing it from becoming a nuisance.
With video content, traffic was consistently good, and there were no strange web ads.
The homepage didn't pop up annoying live streams, so despite the proliferation of live streaming platforms,
Zhao An's platform remained very stable.
The financial crisis was expected to last about two years, and that was an optimistic view.
If things went badly, it might last another year or two.
After all, after debt defaults, insolvency, and even suicides, what would happen to the mess left behind?
Especially in finance, involving lending, violent debt collection, and other chaotic situations.
Every day, there were reports of desperate stock market investors jumping off buildings.
After all, many people had invested heavily during the two-month bull market, even taking out loans.
The situation was incredibly favorable; it was practically a pig could make money.
But what happened?
He built a magnificent mansion, entertained lavishly, and then his mansion collapsed.
"This place is nice; it's worth investing in."
Zhao An lit a cigarette and walked slowly, with Tang Bing and Bai Qingyang beside him.
It was hard to imagine that Bai Qingyang, at the height of his power, would come to see Zhao An.
A scion of a powerful family actually traveled a long way to seek advice from a collateral branch. Interesting. Was he unable to handle things himself and thus seeking guidance?
"You're planning to go into manufacturing?"
Bai Qingyang was somewhat surprised.
After all, the Zhao An he knew had made his fortune in finance; at least in manufacturing, he would believe that real estate would be more profitable.
And in the stock market during the financial crisis, he'd heard that Zhao An hadn't lost money; in fact, he'd made a considerable profit.

"Haha, finance is all hype. Compound interest, money making money—these illusions offer no real benefit. They bring in quick profits, but their foundation is unstable. If something goes wrong, you won't even know how you died. Look at the other three companies, what's become of them? Pfft, they can't even get foreign goods in; they're paralyzed."
Zhao An exhaled a smoke ring, facing a large open space.

"I don't plan on using much real industry here. I'll build a pedestrian street and light industrial factories. This area will become a large farmland, with vegetable processing next to it, and a large cooking center. They'll deliver meals to the company; I'm just improving my employees' benefits and creating some jobs along the way."
Zhao An spoke eloquently. If he were to talk about real industry, it would be the catering sector. People can't live without food, so there will always be profits in food.
"Now that HaoTuan's reputation is ruined, do you want to start from scratch?"
Bai Qingyang had to admire Zhao An; the man was indeed capable and had built a good reputation.
He had supported HaoTuan's food delivery business and then sold it.
Now that the platform's reputation was tarnished and it had become a bloodsucker, it had nothing to do with him.
And people wouldn't be saying, "The dragon-slaying hero has become the dragon himself!"

"No, no, no, don't you understand? In real business, how much money you make doesn't matter. Have you seen my company go public? Those are all scams. Going public is just playing the financial game, and I don't bother with finance. There are so many ways to make money these days. Take online gambling, for example. Do you know how much profit there is? At least 50 billion a year, and that's in US dollars! I know, but I don't do it. Do you know why?"
Zhao An's smile was sinister. Yes, why would he give up such huge profits?
"Why?"
Bai Qingyang vaguely guessed, but wasn't sure.
"That's all thanks to connections with foreign organizations. Otherwise, how could it be set up? What's the use of having so much money? I'm different from you; I only need enough to get by."
Zhao An's smile carried a hint of contempt. Money is indeed always better the more the better.
But what's the use? At a certain point, money is just a number!
"That makes sense."
Bai Qingyang nodded. "Count me in?"
"Go find it in other cities yourself. I'm taking it all here. Developers, businesses—I want it all, I'm not giving it to anyone!"
Zhao An clenched his fist. Why should he give away what he developed?
Besides, stimulating consumption is useless; everything he's doing is turning money that should have been spent into his own profit.
A person needs to eat, drink, and use the restroom. Haircuts, hair dyeing, styling, plus shampoo, shower gel, cosmetics, etc., are all considerable expenses each month.
His idea for creating this pedestrian street was to transform the area into a combined processing and retail space, offering discounts to his employees and other shoppers.
Through word-of-mouth, his brand awareness would gradually grow. He wasn't in a hurry; he didn't rely on it for profit.
It was simply a way to change his public image and establish himself as a true entrepreneur!

chapters.title: Chapter 1196 Dinner
paragraphs: Did he really think that just because he'd played around with so many women he'd forgotten how to make money?
That's impossible. Maintaining a good image is the foundation of his womanizing. Don't women just like young, wealthy men?
As long as they're good-looking and the money's right, they'll all be eager to be taken advantage of!
Bai Qingyang was unconvinced; he was quite satisfied with Zhao An's performance.

Arrogance was irrelevant. As long as there was profit, any arrogance was acceptable. "I'm planning to enter the real estate industry. Now's the perfect time to buy at rock-bottom prices. What do you think?"
"Not a good idea. Real estate isn't profitable unless you can increase construction costs and lower profits."
Zhao An scoffed at real estate; it's all hype...
Once housing prices reach a certain level, they can't rise any higher.
Even if they could rise, how many people could afford to buy?
A very real problem.
Besides, real estate profits are high, but most people rely on loans to buy houses; it's a slow and steady business.
The financial statements certainly look good, but the actual profits are just so-so.
How many people in the real estate industry have massive cash flow?
The two businesses don't overlap, so there's no real competition.
Bai Qingyang came this time to ask Zhao An's opinion, to see what this genius was up to.
Unexpectedly, it's just simple vegetable gardening and cooking—seemingly a return to basics?
This made Bai Qingyang a little disdainful. Had he exhausted his talent?
Nevertheless, Bai Qingyang didn't underestimate Zhao An. They were partners; he could underestimate and despise him, but he couldn't ignore him.
Tang Bing followed behind Zhao An, always with his head down, not because he had any great ability.
But because he unusually fawned over Zhao An, joining his brother Tang Wu in doing so.
Using flattery and offering women to secure survival; otherwise, the Tang family would have been wiped out long ago, and wouldn't exist now.
No one understood Zhao An better than the Tang brothers, Tang Bing and Tang Wu. This man was a devil, an invisible devil.
Every time they thought he was just like that, nothing special, reality would quickly slap them in the face.
The most down-to-earth industries are those that return to simplicity. Business can be down-to-earth, but it can't be down-to-earth.
The financial industry is extremely profitable.
However, once policies change, it's easy to lose everything.
And how many people who rise in the financial industry have clean hands?
The difference lies in whether they want to get involved. When it comes time to withdraw funds, they're easy targets!
The real estate industry's high profits have been mentioned before; it's a slow and steady stream, but the investment is substantial.
Bidding for land, then developing the project—all of these require money.
Then there's the issue of selling the houses; they can't be sold all at once.
Currently, pre-sales are used. The houses are still under construction, but the sales offices are already selling. If the project is abandoned, there's no guarantee of safety.

If pre-sales were abolished, most real estate companies would go bankrupt. Zhao An didn't mention the crucial point: with the financial crisis looming, land purchases with loans would definitely be restricted.
Entering the real estate market now is like joining the German army four or five years ago—suicidal.
After strolling around together, Bai Qingyang only gleaned one key piece of information: focus on real industry. That was all.
He looked at Tang Bing, then at Zhao An.
Zhao An waved his hand. "Tang Bing, prepare a private room. I want to have a good drink and a meal with Young Master Bai."
"Yes, Young Master An."

Tang Bing bowed respectfully, slowly taking four or five steps back until he was a distance from Zhao An. Only then did he turn and leave. This was a sign of respect for his superior, and also for his benefactor.
This kind of etiquette is respectful in a relatively equal social standing setting.
But for someone of vastly different status, it's groveling—groveling to someone stronger than oneself.
The same etiquette, used by different people, has different effects.
Bai Qingyang glanced at Tang Bing, a disdainful smile playing on his lips. "You've trained a pretty good dog."
"Who doesn't have a dog around?"
Zhao An laughed heartily; it was clearly a compliment.
After all, dirty work does need to be done, and that person could be anyone.
There were plenty of people wanting to curry favor with him; women had countless relatives, and there would always be some gossipy aunt or uncle who needed help.
He had the credentials, but he also needed the power.
Without the power and ability, no one could get through.
Zhao An could offer some comfort to the women he had raped.
Returning home in glory is like wearing fine clothes in the dark.
Everyone likes to show off a little.
After all, once you're successful, everyone cares about face.
But offering comfort is one thing...
Zhao An wouldn't be a sucker to take care of others; he could take care of the women's relatives.
But trying to get something for nothing is pure nonsense.
This is just an opportunity, and if the strength required for cooperation isn't up to par, they certainly won't be given that chance.
The two quickly arrived at the hotel, where steaming hot food was served, with a heating device on the table.
Several young men from the provincial capital also came along. They were from a collateral branch of the Bai family, dependent on the Bai family for survival; they could be called lackeys or lackeys.
"This is Li Ming. This is Zhang Lei, this is Wu Bin. You guys take a good look, this is Zhao An. Call him Young Master An. Following him will bring you good fortune."
Bai Qingyang introduced them, picking up the wine bottle and pouring Zhao An a glass.
"Young Master An, I'd like to toast you."
Li Ming picked up his glass and said with a smile. Even Bai Qingyang had to be polite to someone like him; they wouldn't dare to put on airs.
"Come on, everyone."
Zhao An picked up his glass and clinked it with theirs. "What, you want to do business?"
"Haha, we don't have Young Master An's talent. We just run a small company, nothing special."
Zhang Lei laughed loudly, acting all familiar, and offered them cigarettes. "Young Master An, want one?"

Zhao An waved his hand, took out a cigarette himself, and lit it. "I don't smoke other people's cigarettes. Since Bai Qingyang introduced you, there must be something you want to discuss. Just say it. I like to be direct, don't give me any empty promises. When it comes to cooperating with me, I only look at quality, not connections."

Zhang Lei and Li Ming glanced at Bai Qingyang, who simply continued drinking. "Don't look at me. My cooperation with Young Master An is based on quality. I'm just introducing you; whether you can cooperate is up to you. You know better than I do whether you're a dragon or a tiger."
With Bai Qingyang saying this, they had even less to say.
Actually, I was a little unconvinced by Zhao An. What was so arrogant about him?

chapters.title: Chapter 1197 Here to freeload again.
paragraphs: "What kind of business do you all do?"
Zhao An lit a cigarette, swirling his wine glass in one hand, occasionally picking up a bite of food and chewing.
His expression was somewhat nonchalant. He didn't care about these young masters; they were more trouble than they were worth.
If he asked them to help, they might not be able to do anything.
But they could easily sabotage his plans. Most people had no choice but to befriend them, giving them some profits to prevent these parasites from ruining their schemes.
Zhao An, however, was dismissive of this. He might have needed to deal with these people before, but not anymore.
To remain undefeated, his goal wasn't to make money, but to recoup his losses and, incidentally, earn a little extra.
Paying employee salaries was the most significant expense, and Zhao An's task was to recoup all of that.
As mentioned before, people need to eat, drink, and relieve themselves—all of which require money. He could start from there.
He had made a fortune before the financial crisis; it wasn't an exaggeration to say that even if he did nothing, he could live comfortably for three lifetimes.
"I'm in the textile and garment business, Young Master An," Zhang Lei said with a smile, pouring Zhao An some more red wine.
"I'm in the construction team business, Young Master An," Li Ming added with a smile, seemingly with ulterior motives.
"I'm in the cotton farming business, Young Master An," Wu Bin added, his expression calm, neither flattering nor fawning.
Knock, knock, knock. Just then, there was a knock on the door.
"What is it?" Bai Qingyang asked his attendant.
The attendant went to the door to inquire, then returned and said, "Young Master Yang, it's Lin Xiao and Fang Shunli."

"Let them in." Bai Qingyang's heart skipped a beat. It seemed they had also realized the situation and were starting to cooperate with Zhao An, their cheap brother-in-law. He knew about his sister Bai Qiuqin and Zhao An's affair. It wasn't a big deal; marriage was just a formality, while a physical relationship was the real stability.
This was different from those relationships between reporters and female subordinates—it was a stable relationship.
"Haha, Lao Bai, you're not very generous, not even inviting us to dinner. Zhao An, long time no see, we're just here for a free meal, how about you do us a favor?"
Fang Shunli sat down with a smile, the question merely a matter of politeness.
Whether he wanted it or not, he was determined to freeload.
"Long time no see... Zhao An, you've changed a lot in just a few days. You've become even more unpredictable."
Lin Xiao sat down next to Zhao An with a smile, completely oblivious to their previous bitter feud.
"Forget it, I can't tell you're praising me."
Zhao An waved his hand, exhaling a smoke ring. "Just say what you mean, don't give me this pretense."
He was direct, not giving any face. Hypocrisy and politeness were useless.
This kind of behavior is very impolite and would be considered ill-mannered.
It depends on the person.
If it were anyone else, their family would probably have been dealt with by now.
But with Zhao An, there's no need to deal with him. This guy is cunning and shrewd, and he's allied with the Bai family; he's difficult to handle.

"Haha, you haven't changed a bit, still so quick-witted. I came with Brother Fang to apologize to you. This drink is for you. I've offended you in the past, but as the saying goes, 'no discord, no concord.' Everyone has witnessed your abilities. Come on, I'll drink this, you can drink as you like!" Lin Xiao seemingly generously picked up his glass, filled it to the brim—a full two ounces of baijiu—and downed it in one gulp.

"Zhao An, I'll also drink to you. Don't hold grudges about the past. We have different positions. If possible, I'd really like to be friends with you. Come on, I'll drink this, you can drink as you like."
Fang Shunli was also quick to forgive and forget, not caring about losing face; getting the practical benefits first was what mattered.
Zhao An casually picked up his glass and clinked it with theirs, then began to eat and drink heartily, smoking, drinking, and eating seafood, not afraid of causing trouble!

Bai Qingyang, on the other hand, wasn't surprised at all. Not long ago, they were practically mortal enemies, never to speak again; today, they could naturally sit down and drink and eat together. There's no hatred or gratitude between families, only conflicts of interest.
As long as there's profit, everything is negotiable; when it comes to saving face, someone will always find a way to suppress the issue.

Unless it's something like the Southwest Chamber of Commerce, where someone tries to take advantage of another's wife, get her pregnant, and usurp her place—that's a mortal enemy, a hatred that can never be forgiven.
"What brings you all here? Let's skip the simple meal and drinks."
Bai Qingyang said calmly, though he was actually a little displeased. He and Zhao An hadn't even discussed serious matters yet, and these scoundrels had already arrived.
"Haha, the economy's bad, huh? My company's already losing money, not making ends meet. That's why I've come to consult an expert."
Lin Xiao laughed heartily, not using his status as the eldest son of the Lin family to intimidate anyone.
Even if Zhao An didn't give his father face, he didn't care.
"Exactly, we've known each other for a while now. Zhao An's idea, our strength—it's a powerful alliance, what can't we do?"
Fang Shunli's tone was arrogant. Indeed, putting aside the Huang family, the three of them combined could crush them!
As for this kind of thing...
Zhao An had never been interested.

paragraphs: "Japan has six major conglomerates: Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo, Fuji, Sanwa, and Dai-Ichi Kangyo. They control over 60% of Japan's total assets and 50% of its workforce. Calling them zaibatsu isn't an exaggeration; they evolved from zaibatsu. Zaibatsu sounds bad, but conglomerate carries a neutral connotation and sounds much better."
Fang Shunli spoke slowly, showing no lack of business acumen.
"They control the financial, manufacturing, mining, and distribution industries, making it virtually impossible for other small and medium-sized enterprises to get involved.

Mitsubishi, in particular, controls almost 60% of Japan's heavy industry. They can use shares to restrict the development and revenue of their subsidiaries. Their unique annual merit system allows them to continue exploiting their employees... treating them like animals... In their home country, this is called corporate slavery."
Fang Shunli's smile was somewhat sinister, and in truth, it was pretty much true.

Lin Xiao picked up the conversation, "Speaking of their conglomerate model, let's take Japanese conglomerates as an example. They need to control the entire textile industry chain to ensure their dominance. This includes the production of raw materials such as cotton, cashmere, wool, silk, chemical fibers, and down feathers, as well as textile manufacturing of cotton fabrics, chemical fibers, hemp, silk, thread, and dyeing. Then they integrate the downstream industry chain: apparel, home textiles, and industrial textiles. In terms of the overall industry prospects and output value, the best choice is the apparel industry, especially the sportswear industry. This is currently the most promising sector. You can benchmark against Shenzhou..." "Internationally, this is the most profitable company in the entire textile industry."
*Click*
Zhao An continued smoking, nodding. "Not bad, keep going."

"Sanjin, Liucui, Huolan, and other companies are all leaders in the textile industry. Some are in sportswear, some in clothing, and some in cotton textiles. Each field is dominated by top performers. They can easily maintain their position in the industry and then slowly expand into other sectors, seeking steady progress. Clothing design, fashion magazines. Competing with the West for the right to speak in clothing design," Lin Xiao continued.
"There's one thing here: they don't oppose monopolies, but we can't. We can't have monopolies."
Fang Shunli reminded him, afraid that this guy didn't understand what the iron fist of anti-monopoly meant.
If the policy changes, the business might not even break even and would be forced to shut down.
Businessmen still have to do business according to regulations and laws.
After all, the most profitable methods are written in the criminal law.
*Phew!* Zhao An exhaled smoke and downed a glass of red wine.
"What do you think of the current state of the HaoTuan platform?"
The young men from the provincial capital exchanged awkward glances, unsure what to say.
Bai Qingyang and his two companions, however, were deep in thought, puzzled by Zhao An's motives.

"Its reputation is tarnished, its commission rates are too high, it's profiting from others' misfortunes, and its management is ineffective—these are all its shortcomings. Therefore, the platform's traffic has drastically decreased; the dragon-slaying hero has become the dragon himself."
Zhao An chuckled; he had anticipated this situation.
The investment in creating the platform had already been recouped, with a small profit made.
Selling the platform was also a statement, a significant achievement.
"What are your thoughts, Young Master An? Come, let me toast you."
Fang Shunli proactively offered Zhao An a toast. He could endure anything for the sake of profit.
He could sacrifice the interests of his subordinates without hesitation; such a person was truly pragmatic.

"The companies the Huang Group has recently established are quite interesting. Foreign capital holds 40% of the shares and a third of the say. And the businesses they're involved in are all focused on people's livelihoods, including their current plans to expand into lending. These are all financial businesses, industries with inherent instability. Interest compounded, money making money, it's easy for them to collapse."
Zhao An finished speaking and then fell silent, looking at the three men with a half-smile.
"You want us to take him down?"
Lin Xiao's expression also turned serious. It wasn't impossible.
But they had also invested, and they needed to recoup their losses.
Unless their gains exceeded their losses, they absolutely wouldn't do it.
Hearing this, even Fang Shunli's expression changed. Was he trying to pull them into a big heist?
"Hahaha!"
Zhao An laughed loudly, a hint of disdain in his smile.

"You're overthinking it. I don't have time for that. What I'm talking about is their business model. I'm not interested in finance. Finance can certainly make money, a lot of money. But I don't have that idea. I'm saying you can continue to increase your investment. Although the financial industry is in a downturn, you can definitely make a lot of money."
"Oh? What do you mean?"
Bai Qingyang had become interested, but after being put down, he quickly understood and continued to play along.
It was obvious that Fang Shunli and Lin Xiao were two idiots. They hadn't even paid enough, yet they wanted benefits from others. Wasn't that just digging a huge pit for them?
The previous talk about Japanese conglomerates and Korean chaebols was all nonsense; this was the main event.
Originally, he had also become interested in finance, but then he thought about it and realized that this stuff might not be reliable at all.
Fang Shunli and Lin Xiao were indeed somewhat foolish. It wasn't wrong of them to come and talk to them.
But to repair a relationship, at least some sincerity is needed.
They either send women, or they send money and real estate; they always have to give something in return.
They expect to get Zhao An's advice and guidance without spending a penny?
Isn't that a joke?
Perhaps they think that just being able to speak to Zhao An is a favor.
They're trying to get something for nothing, then using this favor as an opportunity for Zhao An.
Although they keep calling him "Young Master An,"
their inherent arrogance is unchangeable.
It's a kind of spiritual contempt, a contempt that can't be concealed from the bone!
Zhao An, of course, knows that if these two sent a celebrity, he might be somewhat interested in cooperating with them.
But that would only be interest, not necessarily cooperation.
But now, he doesn't think that way. These two fools actually dare to try to get something for nothing from him; they're simply courting death.
Have they not learned their lesson enough, so they don't know the meaning of respect?
If we don't teach them a lesson, they won't know what's what!
